I am 75 years old. I only finished primary school, but I have farmed these 5 mu in Quzhou for 55 years, and my father taught me everything before that. I do not need books to tell me what this soil wants. I watch what my neighbors do, and I copy what gives a good harvest.

Last year my wheat gave about 1000 jin per mu and my corn gave about 1200 jin per mu, so I will do almost the same again this year. For wheat, I sow the improved seed that I buy from the county supply store, about 15 kg per mu. Before sowing, I spread three 50-kg bags of compound fertilizer — the one with 15% in each nutrient — across my 5 mu, which is 30 kg per mu. I work it into the soil with the rotary tiller. When the wheat turns green in March, I top-dress three 50-kg bags of urea on the same 5 mu, another 30 kg per mu. I know some people say that is a lot, but I would rather waste some fertilizer than wake up to a thin crop. A bad harvest is a disaster; a few extra yuan on urea is only money. I irrigate three times from my well: the wintering water before the cold comes, the greening water when the wheat wakes up, and the grain-filling water in May. I spray twice: once for weeds in early spring, and once for aphids or rust if I see them on the leaves.

For maize, I plant hybrid seed right after wheat harvest in early June, about 2.5 kg per mu. I put down two 50-kg bags of compound fertilizer on the 5 mu, 20 kg per mu, before sowing. At big trumpet stage, I spread three 50-kg bags of urea, 30 kg per mu. I irrigate twice if the sky does not give rain — once when the plants are knee-high and once when the tassels come out. I spray herbicide once after sowing, and once for corn borer when I see moths flying at night. I rotary till for both crops because two years ago I tried no-till for corn and the wheat straw choked the planter so badly I lost half a day fixing it. Every bag of fertilizer and every hour of pumping costs real money, but I cannot afford to gamble with the crop. My neighbor Lao Zhang does about the same on his 6 mu, and his crops always look green and heavy, so I stick with what works.
